title: OpenAI Defends Safety Firings as Researchers Raise Concerns
source_used: Scripps News and Quasa.io (BankInfoSecurity blocked, HTTP 403)
key_facts: OpenAI said it fired three safety researchers, Tomek Korbak, Jasmine Wang and Mikita Balesni, for a 'breach of trust'.
OpenAI says an investigation found they violated clear policies on handling sensitive information, and that the firings 'were not about safety concerns or speaking out'.
The researchers posted a letter to OpenAI's safety oversight groups saying the firings chill open discussion of safety and urging OpenAI to keep its promise of third-party safety monitors.
Korbak says he was told it was over how he communicated with METR, an independent AI evaluation nonprofit that OpenAI brought in after the July Hugging Face incident.
The Wall Street Journal first reported the firings.
Quasa.io notes the dismissals are confirmed but evidence for either side's explanation is not public.
quote_evidence: OpenAI said on Friday that it fired three safety researchers for a 'breach of trust.'
OpenAI disputed the researchers' version of events, saying the firings 'were not about safety concerns or speaking out.'
why_it_matters_hint: Public dispute at a leading AI lab over safety staff and outside oversight.
event_date: Firings announced 9 Oct 2026; researchers' letter 8 Oct 2026
notes: BankInfoSecurity page blocked; facts from Scripps News (9-10 Oct) and Quasa.io. We could not read what is new on 14 Oct beyond the dispute continuing.
